2607.06681.title: Digital Fragmentation and Generative AI Use Across 103 Million Application Events
2607.06681.paper_summary: Knowledge workers switch between applications thousands of times per day, spending nearly a tenth of the work year transitioning between digital applications in a process called digital fragmentation. Whether this fragmentation reflects who an employee is, where they work, or what kind of day they are having, has remained an open question. We analyzed 103 million application events recorded second-by-second from 1,017 employees across eight organizations that largely employ knowledge workers (e.g., law, financial services). Day-to-day variation in fragmentation within individual employees accounted for 44.6% of the variation in digital fragmentation, slightly exceeding stable individual differences between employees (35.8%), and far exceeding variation between organizations (19.6%). Fragmentation rose over the work week and reset after weekends and holidays. Higher-than-typical use of communication applications coincided with more fragmented work. Generative AI use also occurred on more fragmented days, but the period following AI use was marked by narrower, longer, and more predictable application use. These findings identify the workday as a key level for understanding and intervening on digital fragmentation and suggest that AI may help structure fragmented work rather than merely intensify it.
2607.06681.paper_summary_zh: 知識工作者每天在應用程式之間切換數千次，花費近十分之一的工作年在數位應用程式之間轉換，這一過程稱為數位碎片化。這種碎片化是否反映了員工的身份、工作地點或他們的日常狀況，仍然是一個未解之謎。我們分析了來自八個主要雇用知識工作者的組織（例如法律、金融服務）中1,017名員工記錄的1.03億個應用事件，這些事件是逐秒記錄的。個別員工的日常碎片化變化佔數位碎片化變化的44.6%，略高於員工之間穩定的個體差異（35.8%），並且遠高於組織之間的變化（19.6%）。在工作周內，碎片化隨著時間上升，並在周末和假期後重置。高於典型水平的通訊應用程式使用與更為碎片化的工作同時發生。生成式AI的使用也發生在更為碎片化的日子，但在使用AI後的時期，應用程式的使用變得更為狹窄、持久且可預測。這些發現將工作日確定為理解和介入數位碎片化的關鍵層面，並表明AI可能有助於結構化碎片化的工作，而不僅僅是加劇它。
